**Scenic Relaxed Loop – 4 Days**

**Day 1 – Arrive & settle**  
Fly into SFO, pick up a rental, drive 1 hour 45 min north to Healdsburg. Check into a B&B or vineyard boutique hotel, grab an early dinner at a low-key spot, then call it a day—no early mornings required.

**Day 2 – Russian River Valley**  
Start late morning; the valley is cooler, so the wine walks.  
• Drive east on Highway 153, stop at **Grgich Hills** (open 11 a.m.–5 p.m.), then **La Crema** for a slower pour.  
• Lunch at **Lagunitas Brewing** (pizza and microbrews, casual vibe).  
• Early afternoon: **Stag’s Leap** vineyards—great slopes, easy tasting room.  
• Finish at **Burnt Ridge** for a sunset view, then head back to Healdsburg.

**Day 3 – Central Coast – Paso Robles**  
Drive south ~2.5 hours, break it up with a stop in **Yountville** for coffee and a stroll.  
In Paso, stay at a vineyard cottages or boutique inn:  
• **La Encantada** (11 a.m.–5 p.m., relaxed, no set menus).  
• **Firestone Walker** (next door—brewery plus vineyard, casual, great patio).  
• Optional afternoon: **J. Lohr’s** tasting room; closes at 5 p.m., so you won’t be stuck late.  
• Dinner at a casual spot like **The Golden Oak** (rooftop, no dress code).

**Day 4 – Monterey Peninsula**  
Drive south ~1.5 hours, stop at **San Benito** for a cheap lunch of burgers and beer if you’re hungry.  
• Arrive in Monterey around noon, check into a beachfront B&B or hotel.  
• Afternoon: **Kendall-Jackson** (huge patio, ocean views, à la carte small plates).  
• Evening: stroll Cannery Row, grab seafood tacos or ice cream, then head to sleep—no early morning required.

**Return**: Fly out of SFO or Monterey, whichever is closer to your hotel.

**Key tips**  
• Book tastings ahead, mention “no set menus.”  
• Drive slowly, park at wineries, relax between stops.  
• Keep a cooler in the car for picnic lunches—saves time and money.  
• All routes avoid early mornings; you can sleep in and still hit three solid tasting stops per day.

**Why this works**  
• Loop keeps you within 200 miles of airports.  
• Wineries are spread out so you’re never rushing.  
• Casual, à la carte options everywhere—no forced tasting menus.  
• You can adjust stops daily based on traffic or mood.

Have a great trip.
